1: # The sign-in port answers who is signed in, not where
2: 
3: ADR 0022 moved sign-in into Better Auth and left the WorkOS-shaped `IdentityProvider` in place. That port does two jobs at once: it reads a session, and it asks the provider where the person belongs — an AuthKit organization, an organization-selection prompt, a membership with a role. Better Auth has no organizations at all, and SurveyBeat never wanted the provider to own them (ADR 0006, ADR 0003). This ADR splits the two jobs so the route swap in the next slice has a port to talk to.
4: 
5: **The session port.** `SessionIdentityProvider` in `packages/domain/src/people/SessionIdentity.ts` has two calls: `authenticate(cookie)` returns the `Identity` plus the provider session id, or `Unauthenticated`; `revokeSession(sessionId)` deletes the session. `BetterAuthIdentityProvider` implements it by reading `auth.api.getSession` with the `__Host-surveybeat-session` cookie and, on revoke, deleting the `auth_session` row by id. Nothing is sealed any more: the cookie value is Better Auth's own session token, so a session check costs one D1 read rather than a provider call, and there is no refresh that re-issues a cookie. The WorkOS-shaped `IdentityProvider` keeps serving `/auth/*` until the routes move; then it, `CodeExchange`, `ProviderSession.sealed`, `refresh`, `logoutUrl`, `authorizationUrl` and `authenticateWithCode` are deleted.
6: 
7: **The picker.** A picker only exists because a human can be several Persons. That fact already lives in `people_index` and the Organization's own people table, and `decideSignIn` already builds the candidate list from `PeopleIndex` and `OrganizationPeople`. So the picker stops being a provider concept: no AuthKit organization id, no `OrganizationSelectionRequired`, no pending-authentication token, and no provider round trip when someone chooses. `/auth/organization/choose` resolves the chosen `OrganizationId` against the same candidates and sets nothing in the cookie, because the session is one session across organizations. The `workos_organization_id` column, `organizationByWorkos` and `workosOrganizationOf` go with it.
8: 
9: **Membership.** The provider kept a second copy of membership: `createOrganization`, `ensureMembership`, `setMembershipRole`, `deactivateMembership`. All four leave the port. The Organization is the Durable Object tenant, its `person` rows are the membership, and `organizationAdmin` is a fact in that object (ADR 0003). Nothing writes an admin flag to an auth user, and nothing syncs a role outward, because there is nowhere outward to sync to. The one provider-side id that used to be stored in `people_index` (`auth_user_id`) becomes the Better Auth user id; `PersonId` stays SurveyBeat's own id and `session.user.id` is never treated as one.
10: 
11: **The HTTP surface.** `/auth/logout`, `/auth/session`, `/auth/organization` and `/auth/organization/choose` keep their paths and their responses. `/auth/login` still starts sign-in, but it can no longer redirect to a hosted AuthKit page: the Foldkit app asks for an email address, posts it to Better Auth's code endpoint, and the code returns the session cookie that `/auth/session` already reads. `/auth/callback` exists only because AuthKit redirects, so it goes; the paths in #200 never listed it. Sign-out deletes the session row and answers 303 to the app, since there is no hosted logout page left to redirect to.
12: 
13: **The chosen Organization.** A session is one session across Organizations, so the choice cannot live in the cookie and cannot be an auth-provider concept either. It lives in `auth_session_organization` (`session_id` primary key references `auth_session` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`), one row per session, written only by `/auth/organization/choose` after the choice has been checked against the same candidates. `SessionIdentityProvider` carries `chosenOrganization` and `chooseOrganization`; revoking the session deletes the row with it, and nothing else is ever written. `/auth/session` falls back to the single linked Person when no choice has been made yet, so the first sign-in needs no extra round trip.
14: 
15: **The email code.** The sign-in form needs somewhere to send the address and the code without the browser calling Better Auth directly. `/auth/email-code` and `/auth/email-code/verify` are our own API endpoints; the second hands Better Auth's session token back through `SessionIdentityProvider.verifySignInCode`, and the Worker sets `__Host-surveybeat-session` from it. Everything else under `/auth/*` is Better Auth's own handler, mounted in `MainWorker`.
16: 
17: **Revocation.** Deleting the row is the revocation. `revoked_session`, `isSessionRevoked` and the deny-list half of ADR 0010 are gone: `D1Auth.test.ts` proves a deleted session is refused on the next request while `auth_session_organization` and `person_index` gain no row.
18: 
19: ## Considered options
20: 
21: - **Keep the WorkOS-shaped port and implement it over Better Auth.** Rejected: it would need an authorization URL, an organization-selection exchange and membership writes that Better Auth cannot perform, so the adapter would either lie or die on paths the routes still call.
22: - **Keep the organization picker in the provider by adopting Better Auth's organization plugin.** Rejected in ADR 0022: a second tenant next to the Durable Object.
23: - **Sync Better Auth's user id into `person_index` as the membership key and drop the Person's email lookup.** Rejected: an email still links an unlinked Person before the first sign-in, and `person_index` already holds that evidence.
24: - **Rename `AuthUserId` in the same change as the port.** Rejected for now: the rename touches every domain, D1 and Durable Object call site, and the live WorkOS routes would have to be rewritten twice. The port and the adapter land first; the rename lands with the route swap.
25: 
26: ## Consequences
27: 
28: - `BetterAuthIdentityProvider` and its tests land while WorkOS still serves, so the port is proven against both the in-memory adapter and the real D1 migration before a single route changes.
29: - The route swap is smaller: `AuthHandlers` loses the callback handler and the state cookie, and `MainWorker` provides `SessionIdentityProvider` instead of `IdentityProvider`.
30: - `d1-migrations/0003_people_index.sql` and `0008_better_auth.sql` are rewritten in place: `workos_user_id` is `auth_user_id`, `workos_organization_id` and `revoked_session` are gone, and `auth_session_organization` is new. Any stage that already ran the old files needs its dev schema reset once; the migration history is checked at deploy and refuses a silent rewrite.
31: - The sign-in screen gains an email field, which the web app does not have today; that is the first UI change this issue makes.

1: # Better Auth's magic-link, admin, organization and passkey plugins are enabled
2: 
3: ADR 0022 adopted Better Auth for sign-in with the email one-time-code plugin only, and rejected the organization plugin as the tenant. This ADR adds three more plugins and the passkey plugin to the same instance. The tenant decision does not change: the Organization Durable Object is still the system of record for Teams, People and survey content (ADR 0006), and the plugins are an auth-plane capability rather than a second tenant.
4: 
5: **What is enabled.** `packages/auth/src/options.ts` builds one plugin list for every instance, `authOptions`, so the Worker's `BetterAuth` resource and `createAuth`/`memoryAuth` in tests cannot drift:
6: 
7: - `magicLink` with `MAGIC_LINK_TTL_SECONDS` (300 seconds). The link is delivered through the same `EmailSender` the invitation and sign-in code use, so a non-production stage records it in `captured_email` and production sends it. Better Auth consumes a token on the first verification, so one link mints at most one session.
8: - `admin` with `defaultRole: "user"` and `adminRoles: ["admin"]`. This role is the auth plane's own and is not the Organization admin: Organization admins stay a fact in the Organization object (ADR 0003). No product route reads `user.role`.
9: - `organization` with `allowUserToCreateOrganization: false`. Creating an Organization stays the allowlisted flow in `packages/domain` and the Organization Durable Object; the plugin's `auth_organization`, `auth_member` and `auth_invitation` rows are not the tenant and no product route treats them as one.
10: - `passkey` (`@better-auth/passkey`, pinned with `better-auth`). The relying party is derived from the instance's base URL, so a stage's passkey registrations and the local stage on `localhost` are scoped to their own origin.
11: 
12: **Store.** The plugin columns and tables are a numbered D1 migration, `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/0009_better_auth_plugins.sql`, in the same style as ADR 0022: `auth_user` gains `role`, `banned`, `banReason` and `banExpires`; `auth_session` gains `impersonatedBy` and `activeOrganizationId`; four new tables (`auth_organization`, `auth_member`, `auth_invitation`, `auth_passkey`) keep the `auth_` prefix. Columns and indexes are the schema Better Auth 1.7.11 generates for these plugins with SurveyBeat's model names, so no deploy-time push exists and `migrate: false` still holds.
13: 
14: **Surface.** The Worker forwards every `/auth/*` path it does not answer itself to Better Auth, so the plugin endpoints (`/auth/sign-in/magic-link`, `/auth/magic-link/verify`, `/auth/passkey/*`, `/auth/admin/*`, `/auth/organization/*`) are reachable on the Worker's own origin without a client library. The exact paths SurveyBeat answers, `/auth/organization` and `/auth/organization/choose` among them, keep priority; the plugin's nested routes do not collide with them.
15: 
16: ## Considered options
17: 
18: - **Keep email codes as the only sign-in.** Rejected: the plugins are requested, and a mailed link is the shape that survives a mail client that breaks a code across lines.
19: - **Adopt the organization plugin as the tenant.** Still rejected, for the reason in ADR 0022: two sources of truth for Teams and People.
20: - **Let any signed-in user create a Better Auth organization.** Rejected: Organization creation is allowlisted (`infra/org-creation-allowlist.yaml`), and a second creation path would bypass that list.
21: 
22: ## Consequences
23: 
24: - ADR 0022's "the organization plugin is not adopted" sentence is superseded by this ADR; its other decisions stand.
25: - The mail sender has a second delivery, `sendMagicLink`, beside `sendSignInCode`.
26: - The admin plugin's `banned` flag is enforced by Better Auth on its own endpoints. SurveyBeat's per-request check is unchanged: the Person must be active in the chosen Organization.

9: # Modern Web Guidance

12: 
13: ## Primary Workflow
14: 
15: ### Step 1. Search Use Cases
16: 
17: Run `modern-web-guidance` directly with `npx` using a **2–5 word action-oriented query** for a **single web platform capability or UI pattern**:
18: - **Keep queries focused and generic**: Describe the user-visible capability (`<verb> + <UI/platform object>`, optionally paired with the target HTML/CSS/JS feature name if known). Omit framework/library names (`React`, `Vue`, `Tailwind`, etc.) and app/domain nouns (product, route, or component/file names). Split multi-feature tasks into separate `search` calls.
19: - **Name implied UI primitives**: When the user's prompt expresses intent without naming the UI primitive (e.g. "confirm first", "delete with confirmation", "pick a date"), translate the domain intent into the implied UI component or platform mechanism (e.g. search `"confirmation modal dialog"` or `"confirm dialog"` rather than `"confirm destructive action"`, or `"date picker input"` rather than `"pick a date"`).
20: - **Example**: Search `"light dismiss dialog"` or `"responsive data table"`, **not** `"dialog"` (too terse), `"responsive table dark mode"` (compound — split into two searches), or `"close React settings modal on outside click"` (framework/app noise).

24: ```

29: > - **Topic not covered**: If no `description` matches after rephrasing, proceed without retrieving unrelated guides.

You can pass multiple IDs separated by commas.

To read the rest of this line range, call this tool again with the same StartLine and EndLine and ByteOffset=46080. 1: --- Guide for passkeys --- 2: # Passkeys Orientation 3: 4: This guide provides high-density, action-oriented orientation for implementing secure, framework-agnostic passkey authentication and credential management in modern web applications. 5: 6: ## 1. Core Prerequisites for Passkeys 7: 8: Passkeys rely on the Web Authentication API (WebAuthn), which imposes strict cross-cutting security constraints that must be satisfied before any implementation attempt: 9: * **Secure Contexts**: WebAuthn methods (`navigator.credentials.create` and `navigator.credentials.get`) are strictly gated behind Secure Contexts. Applications MUST run on `https://` in production, or `http://localhost` for local development. 10: * **Relying Party (RP) ID**: Every credential is tied to an RP ID (essentially the domain name of the application). The RP ID passed in the server-side options MUST match or be a valid registrable domain suffix of the current origin's domain name (e.g., `example.com` is valid for `login.example.com`), or be authorized via Related Origin Requests (`/.well-known/webauthn`). Mismatches result in `SecurityError` exceptions on the client side. **DO NOT** derive `rpId` from `window.location.hostname` on the client (for example, when calling WebAuthn Signal API methods), because `window.location.hostname` will not match a parent-domain or related-origin RP ID configured on the server; always read `rpId` from the server-provided WebAuthn options (`publicKey.rp.id` or `publicKey.rpId`) or backend API responses. 11: 12: ## 2. The AAGUID UX Caveat 13: 14: The Authenticator Attestation Globally Unique Identifier (AAGUID) is a 128-bit identifier returned in the registration attestation data that represents the model/provider of the authenticator (e.g., Google Password Manager, iCloud Keychain, 1Password). 15: * **UX Hinting Only**: Relying Parties MUST use the AAGUID exclusively for UX hints (such as rendering the passkey provider name and icon in a management list to help the user). 16: * **No Security Dependencies**: applications MUST NOT use AAGUID for cryptographic security or access decisions. Platform passkeys do not currently provide cryptographic attestation for their AAGUIDs, meaning it can be altered or simulated by user agents. 17: 18: ## 3. Decoupled Library Recommendations 19: 20: For backend FIDO2/WebAuthn options generation and signature verification, developers MUST rely on vetted open source libraries per language instead of hand-rolling cryptography: 21: * **JavaScript/TypeScript**: SimpleWebAuthn (github.com/MasterKale/SimpleWebAuthn) 22: * **Python**: py_webauthn (github.com/duo-labs/py_webauthn) 23: * **Java**: Java WebAuthn Server (github.com/Yubico/java-webauthn-server), WebAuthn4J (github.com/webauthn4j/webauthn4j) 24: * **.NET**: .NET library for FIDO2 (github.com/abergs/fido2-net-lib) 25: * **Go**: WebAuthn Go Library (github.com/go-webauthn/webauthn) 26: * **Ruby**: WebAuthn Ruby (github.com/cedarcode/webauthn-ruby) 27: * **PHP**: WebAuthn Framework (github.com/web-auth/webauthn-framework) 28: 29: ## 4. Use Case Reference Matrix 30: 31: Identify the matching use case below and retrieve its full implementation guide. Every use case has critical APIs (`PublicKeyCredential.parseCreationOptionsFromJSON`, `parseRequestOptionsFromJSON`, `signalAllAcceptedCredentials`, `signalCurrentUserDetails`, `signalUnknownCredential`, conditional mediation, AAGUID handling, etc.) that are documented only in the per-use-case guide. Do NOT skip this retrieval step, and do NOT substitute third-party library wrappers (such as SimpleWebAuthn's `startAuthentication`/`startRegistration`) on the client — call the native WebAuthn browser APIs directly. Library recommendations in Section 3 apply to the **server-side** (backend FIDO2 verification) only. 32: 33: Specific passkey and WebAuthn implementation details are mapped to the following guides: 34: * **Passkey Registration**: `passkey-registration` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "passkey-registration"`) — Offering new passkey registration and promotions. 35: * **Passkey Conditional Create**: `passkey-conditional-create` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "passkey-conditional-create"`) — Silently registering passkeys immediately after successful password login. 36: * **Passkey Authentication**: `passkey-authentication` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "passkey-authentication"`) — Discoverable-autofill and button sign-ins. 37: * **Quick Sign-Ins**: `quick-sign-ins` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "quick-sign-ins"`) — Contextual in-place sign-ins with local passkeys and saved passwords before page navigation. 38: * **Passkey Management**: `passkey-management` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "passkey-management"`) — Syncing lists, renames, and deletions with password managers. 39: * **Passkey Reauthentication**: `passkey-reauthentication` (via `npx -y modern-web-guidance@latest retrieve "passkey-reauthentication"`) — Re-verifying returning signed-in users for sensitive steps. 40: 41: 42: 43: --- Guide for passkey-authentication --- 44: # Passkey Authentication 45: 46: This guide details how to implement returning user authentication using discoverable credentials, both through explicit button triggers and seamless browser autofill suggestions (Conditional UI). 47: 48: ## Server-Side 49: 50: ### Options Generation 51: 52: Create an endpoint that generates WebAuthn request parameters using a vetted library per standards. 53: 54: 1. **Use the predefined RP ID**: Use the predefined proper RP ID as a constant string and include it as `rpId` in the returned request options so the client can pass `publicKey.rpId` directly to Signal API calls. 55: 2. **Generate challenge**: Generate a high-entropy, cryptographically secure random buffer, store it securely in the user's session, and encode it as Base64URL. 56: 3. **Discoverable Credentials mapping**: Specify an empty array `[]` for `allowCredentials`. This requests discoverable credentials, meaning the user does not need to enter their username first; the passkey provider will present available accounts. 57: 4. **User Verification level**: Set `userVerification: "preferred"` (or `"required"` if explicitly mandated by corporate compliance policies). 58: - The requested `userVerification` constraint level MUST be persisted inside the server session record at the options endpoint, rather than passed back from the client via query strings. This allows the verification endpoint to enforce strict matching constraints safely without risk of client manipulation. 59: 60: ```javascript 61: // Options generation example (discoverable flow) 62: const options = { 63: challenge: serverGeneratedBase64UrlChallenge, // High-entropy random challenge stored in session 64: rpId: "example.com", 65: allowCredentials: [], // Request discoverable passkeys 66: userVerification: "preferred", 67: }; 68: 69: // Persist expected UV level to user session 70: req.session.expectedUserVerification = "preferred"; 71: ``` 72: 73: ### Verification Endpoint 74: 75: Securely verify the assertion returned by the client to authenticate the user: 76: 77: 1. **Validate session challenge**: Enforce strict challenge matching between the client response and the expected challenge stored in the session. 78: 2. **Enforce UV Preferences**: 79: - Allow UV-less authenticators (e.g., authenticator screen locks disabled) if the session's `expectedUserVerification` requested `"preferred"`, by passing `requireUserVerification: false` to your server-side verification library. If requested `"required"`, enforce biometrics/PIN entry strictly. 80: 3. **Clean Server Error 404**: If the credential ID returned by the client is not found in the database, return an explicit HTTP `404` error so the client can trigger the Signal API. 81: 82: ## Client-Side Logic 83: 84: ### HTML Form Annotation 85: 86: Annotate your username and password inputs to natively leverage Conditional UI. Autocomplete tokens combine the webauthn spec parameters. 87: 88: Use the `autofocus` attribute on dedicated sign-in pages and sign-in dialogs so that the autofill options are immediately displayed. Do not use the `autofocus` attribute on pages or dialogs that are not dedicated sign-in forms. Do not use the `autofocus` attribute on sign-in forms that are embedded in a larger page. Ensure that pages have a concise but descriptive page title, and that dialogs have a concise but descriptive accessible name when the `autofocus` attribute is used on dedicated sign-in pages and dialogs. 89: 90: Use the `aria-describedby` attribute on elements with `autofocus` so instructions and context are provided for screen reader users. 91: 92: ```html 93:

Sign In with Passkey

94: 95:
96: 104: 105: 106:

The `MainWorker.ts` file, specifically lines 157-161, shows a crucial interaction point. It appears to be where several libraries interact. Reviewing the interactions.


The `BetterAuth` instantiation in `MainWorker.ts` lacks explicit `baseURL` or `trustedOrigins` configuration. Examining the `authOptions` function reveals default trusted origins, but these are overridden by the environment. If the `baseURL` is not set, a passkey-related issue may occur. The missing configuration likely prevents proper communication in development and staging environments.


The `getRpID` function's reliance on a missing `baseURL` within `MainWorker.ts` defaults to "localhost," which invalidates passkey authentication in deployed environments. This configuration flaw would manifest as a security error, because the relying party ID ("localhost") does not match the actual domain (e.g., dashboard.surveybeat.app). 1: import { type Equivalence, Option, Schema, Stream } from 'effect';
2: type SubscriptionBrand = {
3:     readonly __subscription: never;
4: };
5: type DependenciesSchema<Dependencies> = Schema.Schema<Dependencies> & {
6:     readonly fields: Schema.Struct.Fields;
7: };
8: /**
9:  * The entry shape produced by helpers like `Subscription.persistentEntry` and
10:  * `Port.subscriptionEntry` before branding. Pass values of this shape into
11:  * `Subscription.make` as entry values.
12:  */
13: export type EntryWithoutKeepAlive<Model, Message, Dependencies, Services> = {
14:     readonly dependenciesSchema: DependenciesSchema<Dependencies>;
15:     readonly modelToDependencies: (model: Model) => Dependencies;
16:     readonly keepAliveEquivalence?: never;
17:     readonly dependenciesToStream: (dependencies: Dependencies) => Stream.Stream<Message, never, Services>;
18: };
19: type EntryWithKeepAlive<Model, Message, Dependencies, Services> = {
20:     readonly dependenciesSchema: DependenciesSchema<Dependencies>;
21:     readonly modelToDependencies: (model: Model) => Dependencies;
22:     readonly keepAliveEquivalence: Equivalence.Equivalence<Dependencies>;
23:     readonly dependenciesToStream: (dependencies: Dependencies, readDependencies: () => Dependencies) => Stream.Stream<Message, never, Services>;
24: };
25: type Entry<Model, Message, Dependencies, Services = never> = EntryWithoutKeepAlive<Model, Message, Dependencies, Services> | EntryWithKeepAlive<Model, Message, Dependencies, Services>;
26: /**
27:  * A single subscription entry produced by `Subscription.make`,
28:  * `Subscription.lift`, or `Subscription.aggregate`. The brand field is
29:  * `never`, so application code cannot manually construct a `Subscription`
30:  * value: it must go through one of those constructors (or a helper like
31:  * `Subscription.persistentEntry` that returns an entry shape, then through
32:  * `make`).
33:  *
34:  * Two variants by `keepAliveEquivalence` presence:
35:  *
36:  * - Without `keepAliveEquivalence` (the common case), every Model change recomputes
37:  *   the dependencies. Equivalent dependencies leave the Stream alone; any
38:  *   change tears it down and restarts. `dependenciesToStream` takes a single
39:  *   argument: the latest dependencies.
40:  * - With `keepAliveEquivalence` (an escape hatch), Model changes that the
41:  *   equivalence treats as equal leave the Stream running, but the running
42:  *   Stream can still read the latest dependencies via the second
43:  *   `readDependencies` argument. Use this when the Stream needs mid-flight
44:  *   access to data that changes often but shouldn't trigger restarts
45:  *   (Foldkit UI's `DragAndDrop.autoScroll` reading the latest pointer
46:  *   `clientY` each rAF tick is the canonical example).
47:  *
48:  * `dependenciesSchema` must be a `Schema.Struct` so every dependency is
49:  * explicitly named at the schema level.
50:  */
51: export type Subscription<Model, Message, Dependencies, Services = never> = Entry<Model, Message, Dependencies, Services> & SubscriptionBrand;
52: /** A record of named Subscriptions keyed by dependency field name. */
53: export type Subscriptions<Model, Message, Services = never> = Readonly<Record<string, Subscription<Model, Message, any, Services>>>;
54: /**
55:  * Callbacks for a subscription entry without `keepAliveEquivalence`. Dependencies
56:  * are inferred from the field map passed to `entry`.
57:  */
58: type EntryCallbacksWithoutKeepAlive<Model, Message, Dependencies, Services> = {
59:     readonly modelToDependencies: (model: Model) => Dependencies;
60:     readonly keepAliveEquivalence?: never;
61:     readonly dependenciesToStream: (dependencies: Dependencies) => Stream.Stream<Message, never, Services>;
62: };
63: /**
64:  * Callbacks for a subscription entry with `keepAliveEquivalence`. Dependencies
65:  * are inferred from the field map passed to `entry`.
66:  */
67: type EntryCallbacksWithKeepAlive<Model, Message, Dependencies, Services> = {
68:     readonly modelToDependencies: (model: Model) => Dependencies;
69:     readonly keepAliveEquivalence: Equivalence.Equivalence<Dependencies>;
70:     readonly dependenciesToStream: (dependencies: Dependencies, readDependencies: () => Dependencies) => Stream.Stream<Message, never, Services>;
71: };
72: /**
73:  * Builds a single subscription entry from a field map and callbacks.
74:  *
75:  * The field map is the same shape you would pass to `Schema.Struct`. Reading the
76:  * schema as a positional argument (rather than a property on the entry
77:  * literal) lets TypeScript fully resolve the `Dependencies` type before
78:  * contextually typing `modelToDependencies` and `dependenciesToStream`, so
79:  * destructuring patterns like `({ maybeMapHostId })` are inferred correctly
80:  * even when the field schemas use transforms (e.g. `Schema.Option`).
81:  *
82:  * Two overloads, one per `keepAliveEquivalence` presence:
83:  *
84:  * - Without `keepAliveEquivalence`, `dependenciesToStream` takes a single
85:  *   `dependencies` argument.
86:  * - With `keepAliveEquivalence`, `dependenciesToStream` also receives a
87:  *   `readDependencies` thunk for accessing the latest value while the Stream
88:  *   stays running across Model changes the equivalence accepts as equal.
89:  */
90: export type EntryBuilder<Model, Message, Services> = <const Fields extends Schema.Struct.Fields, Callbacks extends EntryCallbacksWithoutKeepAlive<Model, Message, Schema.Struct.Type<Fields>, Services> | EntryCallbacksWithKeepAlive<Model, Message, Schema.Struct.Type<Fields>, Services>>(fields: Fields, callbacks: Callbacks) => Callbacks extends {
91:     readonly keepAliveEquivalence: Equivalence.Equivalence<any>;
92: } ? EntryWithKeepAlive<Model, Message, Schema.Struct.Type<Fields>, Services> : EntryWithoutKeepAlive<Model, Message, Schema.Struct.Type<Fields>, Services>;
93: /**
94:  * Declares a Subscriptions record. The Model, Message, and optional Services
95:  * generics are provided up front; the entries record follows, built from
96:  * calls to the `entry` builder passed into the inner function.
97:  *
98:  * Reach for `Subscription.aggregate` to combine multiple records, and
99:  * `Subscription.lift` to translate a child Submodel's record into a parent
100:  * context.
101:  *
102:  * @example
103:  * ```ts
104:  * Subscription.make<Model, Message>()(entry => ({
105:  *   tick: entry(
106:  *     { isRunning: Schema.Boolean },
107:  *     {
108:  *       modelToDependencies: model => ({ isRunning: model.isRunning }),
109:  *       dependenciesToStream: ({ isRunning }) =>
110:  *         Stream.when(..., Effect.sync(() => isRunning)),
111:  *     },
112:  *   ),
113:  * }))
114:  * ```
115:  */
116: export declare const make: <Model, Message, Services = never>() => <Entries extends Readonly<Record<string, Entry<Model, Message, any, Services>>>>(build: (entry: EntryBuilder<Model, Message, Services>) => Entries) => { readonly [K in keyof Entries]: Entries[K] & SubscriptionBrand; };
117: type AnySubscriptions = Readonly<Record<string, Subscription<any, any, any, any>>>;
118: type AnySubscriptionsList = readonly [
119:     AnySubscriptions,
120:     ...ReadonlyArray<AnySubscriptions>
121: ];
122: type EntriesOfRecord<SubscriptionsRecord> = SubscriptionsRecord extends unknown ? SubscriptionsRecord[keyof SubscriptionsRecord] : never;
123: type EntriesOf<Records extends AnySubscriptionsList> = EntriesOfRecord<Records[number]>;
124: type ModelOfEntry<AnyEntry> = [AnyEntry] extends [
125:     Subscription<infer Model, any, any, any>
126: ] ? unknown extends Model ? never : Model : never;
127: type MessageOfEntry<AnyEntry> = AnyEntry extends Subscription<any, infer Message, any, any> ? Message : never;
128: type ServicesOfEntry<AnyEntry> = AnyEntry extends Subscription<any, any, any, infer Services> ? Services : never;
129: type MessageOf<Records extends AnySubscriptionsList> = MessageOfEntry<EntriesOf<Records>>;
130: type ServicesOf<Records extends AnySubscriptionsList> = ServicesOfEntry<EntriesOf<Records>>;
131: type ReferenceModel<Records extends ReadonlyArray<AnySubscriptions>> = Records extends readonly [
132:     infer Head extends AnySubscriptions,
133:     ...infer Rest extends ReadonlyArray<AnySubscriptions>
134: ] ? [ModelOfEntry<EntriesOfRecord<Head>>] extends [never] ? ReferenceModel<Rest> : ModelOfEntry<EntriesOfRecord<Head>> : never;
135: type CompatibleSubscriptions<Records extends AnySubscriptionsList> = {
136:     readonly [Index in keyof Records]: Records[Index] & Subscriptions<ReferenceModel<Records>, MessageOf<Records>, ServicesOf<Records>>;
137: };
138: type RuntimeKey<Key> = Key extends string ? Key : Key extends number ? `${Key}` : never;
139: type RuntimeEntries<RecordType> = {
140:     readonly [Key in keyof RecordType as RuntimeKey<Key>]: RecordType[Key];
141: };
142: type MergeSubscriptions<Records extends ReadonlyArray<unknown>> = Records extends readonly [infer Head, ...infer Rest] ? RuntimeEntries<Head> & (Rest extends ReadonlyArray<unknown> ? MergeSubscriptions<Rest> : {}) : {};
143: /**
144:  * Combines multiple Subscriptions records into one. Throws on duplicate
145:  * keys so a misconfigured aggregate fails loudly at startup rather than
146:  * silently overriding.
147:  *
148:  * Pass the records directly and the Model, Message, and Services are read
149:  * off them. The Model of the first record with a Model dependency is the one
150:  * every later record is checked against, so a record from another Model
151:  * universe fails at its own argument position. Message and Services widen to
152:  * the union across all records, which is what lets a record that needs an
153:  * Effect service sit beside records that need none.
154:  *
155:  * The result keeps each record's keys and each entry's exact dependency type,
156:  * schema, and `keepAliveEquivalence` variant, so a lifted entry's
157:  * {@link GatedDependencies} survives aggregation.
158:  *
159:  * The curried form remains available for a record that has to be typed before
160:  * its entries exist, such as a value annotated as
161:  * `Subscriptions<Model, Message>` at a module boundary. It erases keys and
162:  * per-entry dependency types, so reach for it only when the explicit contract
163:  * is the point.
164:  *
165:  * @example
166:  * ```ts
167:  * const subscriptions = Subscription.aggregate(
168:  *   homeSubscriptions,
169:  *   roomSubscriptions,
170:  * )
171:  * ```
172:  *
173:  * @example Curried, when the record is typed before its entries exist:
174:  * ```ts
175:  * export const subscriptions: Subscription.Subscriptions<Model, Message> =
176:  *   Subscription.aggregate<Model, Message>()(...records)
177:  * ```
178:  */
179: export declare const aggregate: {
180:     <Model, Message, Services = never>(): (...records: ReadonlyArray<Subscriptions<Model, Message, Services>>) => Subscriptions<Model, Message, Services>;
181:     <Records extends AnySubscriptionsList>(...records: CompatibleSubscriptions<Records>): MergeSubscriptions<Records>;
182: };
183: /**
184:  * Wraps a Stream as a Subscription entry with no dependencies on its own
185:  * Model. Local Model changes do not restart the Stream. A parent can still
186:  * gate the entry when lifting it, so the Stream starts and stops with that
187:  * parent condition. Use for work such as system theme listeners, viewport
188:  * width observers, or route-independent timers.
189:  *
190:  * Returns an entry shape, not a branded Subscription. Pass it into `make`
191:  * as an entry value.
192:  */
193: export declare const persistentEntry: <Message, Services = never>(stream: Stream.Stream<Message, never, Services>) => EntryWithoutKeepAlive<unknown, Message, Record<string, never>, Services>;
194: type ChildModelOf<ChildSubscriptions> = ChildSubscriptions[keyof ChildSubscriptions] extends Subscription<infer ChildModel, any, any, any> ? ChildModel : never;
195: type ChildMessageOf<ChildSubscriptions> = ChildSubscriptions[keyof ChildSubscriptions] extends Subscription<any, infer ChildMessage, any, any> ? ChildMessage : never;
196: /**
197:  * The dependencies of a lifted Subscription. `maybeDependencies` holds the
198:  * child's dependencies while `read` returns `Some` and its `when` gate is
199:  * open. Otherwise it holds `None`, which tears down the entry's Stream and
200:  * skips the child's `modelToDependencies`.
201:  */
202: export type GatedDependencies<Dependencies> = Readonly<{
203:     maybeDependencies: Option.Option<Dependencies>;
204: }>;
205: type WhenPredicate<ParentModel> = (parentModel: ParentModel) => boolean;
206: /**
207:  * Additional parent conditions for named entries in a lift's `when` map.
208:  * Entries omitted from the map run whenever `read` returns a child Model.
209:  */
210: export type EntryGates<ParentModel, Subscriptions> = Readonly<Partial<Record<keyof Subscriptions, WhenPredicate<ParentModel>>>>;

212:     read: (parentModel: ParentModel) => Option.Option<ChildModelOf<Subscriptions>>;
213:     toParentMessage: (message: ChildMessageOf<Subscriptions>) => ParentMessage;
214:     when?: WhenPredicate<ParentModel> | EntryGates<ParentModel, Subscriptions>;
215: }>;

217:     readonly [K in keyof Subscriptions]: Subscriptions[K] extends Subscription<any, any, infer Dependencies, infer Services> ? Subscription<ParentModel, ParentMessage, GatedDependencies<Dependencies>, Services> : never;

## Signal API Synchronization

The Signal API lets the application communicate credential states to password managers, keeping the user's synced vaults and your backend database in lockstep.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Browsers strictly validate Base64URL encoding and string length (`length % 4 !== 1`, characters strictly `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`, no `=` padding) in native code. Passing arbitrary human-readable placeholder or mock IDs (such as `'passkey-1'`, `'cred:01'`, or unencoded strings like `'cred_yubikey_01'`) throws `TypeError: Invalid base64url string for allAcceptedCredentialIds` on page load. Always encode mock/test IDs as genuine unpadded Base64URL strings (for example, `'dGVzdC1jcmVkLTE'` or `Buffer.from('cred-1').toString('base64url')`) and validate format before invoking the Signal API.

*   **Use the Server-Provided `rpId` (DO NOT Use `window.location.hostname`)**:
    *   Always pass the `rpId` returned by your backend API (matching the `rp.id` used when registering passkeys). **DO NOT** derive `rpId` from `window.location.hostname` on the client: when credentials are registered to a registrable parent domain (for example, `example.com` while the settings page is served on `accounts.example.com`) or shared via Related Origin Requests (`/.well-known/webauthn`), `window.location.hostname` will not match the credential's RP ID, causing password manager synchronization to silently target the wrong RP ID or throw a `SecurityError`.
*   **Feature Detection & Parameter Encoding Rule**:
    *   Always feature-detect Signal API methods before invoking them (`if (PublicKeyCredential.signalAllAcceptedCredentials)` and `if (PublicKeyCredential.signalCurrentUserDetails)`).

    *   Signal API calls perform passive background synchronization and MUST NOT break the UI or emit `console.error` when synchronization fails.
